contentHtml:
Chennai: A 30-year-old chartered accountant has been arrested in Chennai for allegedly diverting approximately Rs 8.2 crore from his former employer, a pharmaceutical firm, into 44 bank accounts in Andhra Pradesh through 95 transactions between 2021 and 2023.

Police officials stated that the recipient accounts were linked to his close family members and relatives, while the entire misappropriated amount remains unrecovered.

According to the recent media report in The420, the Entrustment Document Fraud (EDF) wing of the Central Crime Branch identified the accused as S. Sudhir Gatiganti, a resident of Noombal near Porur. He was arrested on Saturday in connection with the alleged financial irregularities at a pharmaceutical company located in Pattaravakkam near Avadi. According to police officials, preliminary findings indicate that the accused’s family members were unaware of his alleged financial misconduct.

Investigators revealed that Gatiganti initially joined the pharmaceutical firm as an accountant in 2018. During his employment, he gradually advanced in his career and was eventually promoted to the position of finance manager.

He continued working in the organization until he resigned in 2024. During his tenure, the accused reportedly held significant authority over the company’s financial operations and disbursement procedures. His responsibilities included distributing cheques and releasing payments to the firm’s suppliers. This position provided him with direct access to company funds and payment authorization workflows.

Investigators suspect that he misused the authority entrusted to him to divert money from the company’s corporate account into personal bank accounts and accounts belonging to his relatives over a period of two years. The alleged transactions were carried out between 2021 and 2023.

The alleged financial misconduct came to light after suppliers began raising complaints regarding discrepancies in their payments. By that time,the accused had already resigned from the organization in 2024,and the company had appointed a new finance manager. Following the complaints,the management initiated an internal scrutiny of the company’s financial records. The examination subsequently uncovered unauthorized transfers amounting to approximately Rs 8.2 crore.

According to police officials,the accused allegedly carried out 95 separate transactions,transferring the money into 44 bank accounts located in Andhra Pradesh. These accounts were reportedly associated with his close family members and relatives. However,current evidence does not indicate that these individuals were aware of or involved in the alleged embezzlement. Law enforcement agencies are examining transaction records and bank statements to establish the exact movement of the diverted funds and identify their ultimate destinations.

Police officials also noted that the accused is married and has a six-month-old child. Despite the arrest,authorities confirmed that none of the allegedly misappropriated Rs 8.2 crore has been recovered so far. Investigating agencies are currently tracing the movement of the money across the linked bank accounts to determine how the funds were utilized after being transferred. The investigation is also examining the financial transactions associated with the accounts belonging to the accused’s relatives.

According to a report by The420,authorities have not yet disclosed further details regarding potential asset freezes,recovery timelines or the possible involvement of other individuals in the alleged fraud. The Central Crime Branch is continuing its investigation,with further questioning and financial audits underway to establish the complete extent of the financial irregularities.

The case highlights the importance of robust financial monitoring,internal auditing and payment authorization controls within pharmaceutical companies to prevent the misuse of financial authority and unauthorized diversion of corporate funds.
